sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
கொடியிடைக் கிடந்தாளை கொடியிடையாளை
நொடியிடை கரம் பிடித்த கந்தா
sections.translit:
kodiyidaik kidandhALai kodiyidaiyALai
nodiyidai karam pidittha kandhA
sections.en: Skanda, in a split second, you picked up the hand of the slender tribal girl Valli. When Valli was a baby she used to lay by the side of a creeper plant by the same name.

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
தேவசேனை பதியாய் சென்று அமரினில் வென்று
தேவயானை பதியான தேவாதி தேவா
sections.translit:
dhEvasEnai pathiyAy sendRu amarinil vendRu
dhEvayAnai pathiyAna dhEvAdhi dEvA
sections.en: You are the God of Gods,  the head of a celestial army who won a tough fight with the demon Soorapadman. As a gift, you wedded Deivayanai, the daughter of Indra, chief of demigods.

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
பொய்கை அருகே கடுந்தவம் புரிந்தாரென
பொய்யாது வந்தவரை மணந்தாய் உனையே
ஓயாது நினைந்து இப்பிறவி போதும் என்று
மாயாது நிற்கும் எனை ஆளவாராயோ ஐயனே
sections.translit:
poygai arugE kadunthavam purindhArena
poyyAdhu vandhavarai maNandhAy unaiyE
OyAdhu ninaindhu ippiRavi pOdhum endRu
mAyAdhu niRkum enai ALavArAyO aiyanE
sections.en: You married two sisters, Valli and Deivayanai, recognizing that they did serious penance in their previous birth near the divine Saravana pond. Won’t you come now and take me into your fold, this poor soul who is constantly thinking of you and is yet to leave this mortal coil?

notes: The charanam of this song incorporates the story of Mahavishnu’s daughters, Amritavalli and Sundaravalli, who longed to marry Lord Shanmuga (Muruga) and performed severe penance on the banks of the sacred pond Saravana Poigai. Pleased with their devotion, Lord Muruga blessed them and promised to marry them at an appropriate time. In their next birth, Amritavalli was raised by Indra, the Lord of the Devas, while her younger sister Sundaravalli was born as the daughter of Sage Sivamuni amidst the valli creeper plants and was brought up by Nambi, the chief of the Veddas (hunters). Amritavalli, constantly in the company of Indra’s elephant Iravatham, came to be known as Devayanai. The tribal chief, Nambi, named the baby girl Sundaravalli, as she was found lying among the valli creepers (வள்ளி). The pallavi of the song depicts Muruga’s arrival in the millet field to marry Valli at a destined time. Disguised as a hunter, Muruga performed several mystical acts. After a brief verbal exchange with Valli, the Lord appeared as an old man and engaged in flirtatious behavior. The old man asked Valli for some food, and she offered him millet flour and mountain honey. Pretending to choke and suffer hiccoughs from the dry flour, he requested water. Valli led him to a nearby waterfall to drink. The moment he quenched his thirst, Muruga grasped her hand and expressed his love. When Valli refused, Muruga meditated upon his elder brother, Ganesha, who appeared in the form of a wild elephant. Terrified by the charging elephant, Valli clung to the old man for protection and, in her fear, agreed to marry him. At that moment, Muruga revealed His true divine form, and the two fell instantly in love. Nambi rejoiced upon hearing that his daughter had fallen in love with Lord Siva’s son and arranged their marriage. According to the sthalapuranam of the Thiruttani Murugan Temple, Muruga brought Valli from Vallimalai (where she was raised) and married her there. Devotees celebrate this Valli Kalyanam for ten days every year at the temple. The anupallavi of the song refers to Devayanai’s wedding. After slaying the demon Soorapadman, Muruga arrived at Thirupparankundram, where, with the blessings of His parents and the other celestials, He fulfilled His promise by marrying Devayanai. The divine Lord finally attained peace after his battle with Soorapadman at Thiruttanigai. Muruga weds Valli and Devayanai Valli, Muruga’s wedding reenacted in Thiruttani Muruga’s abode , Thiruttani Subramanya Swamy Temple Sthalapuranam
